catalog_quote: 2.4. Les tons. Le système tonal comporte trois niveaux de tons ponctuels: haut (H), moyen (M), bas (B) et deux types de tons complexes: bas-haut (BH), haut-bas (HB). Avec voyelle longue ... on rencontre également des séquences: haut-moyen (H-M), moyen-moyen (M-M), bas-moyen (B-M) mais ce ne sont pas des tons lexicaux de la langue. ... (p. 201) La grande majorité des verbes a un schème tonal lexical linéaire: haut (H), moyen (M) ou bas (B), c'est-à-dire que ces verbes ont les mêmes tons lexicaux sur toutes leurs syllabes, ou un ton ponctuel pour les monoverbes. ... Le ton lexical apparaît clairement à l'aoriste. [table: H ʔyá 'tuer', M ʔyā 'se coucher', B yà 'donner naissance']

new_statements.second_reader_evidence: Only one work was listed for this item, so a two-work spot-check was not possible; the single listed work was checked in full as above. I also spot-checked the on-disk comparison sources the compiler leaned on: Barreteau & Jungraithmayr 1982 'Le verbe en sibine' ( lines 11086-13500) has no 'accent', 'stress', 'intensite' or 'tonique' token; its sec. 2.4 Les tons (printed p. 197) gives three level tones H/M/B plus BH and HB contours and no accent statement. The 'accent' passages at lines 5566-5828 (position de l'accent, accent d'intensite) belong to Jouannet's chapter 'Accompli et Inaccompli en Kanembou', a Saharan language, not to Sibine, so they must not be read as Somrai evidence. tone_statements.citation: Jungraithmayr, Herrmann. 2024. Emergenz und Genese der Tonalität im Tschadischen: Ein Beitrag zur Sprachgeschichte Nordostafrikas [Emergence and genesis of tonality in Chadic: a contribution to the linguistic history of Northeast Africa]. Folia Orientalia 61: 167-192. doi:10.24425/for.2024.152390 (CC BY 4.0).
tone_statements.quote: Überquert man den Schari und betritt den Boden des Zweistromlandes (Land zwischen Schari und Logone), das in seinem oberen Teil (bis etwa 9. Grad n. Br. im Süden) ausschließlich von tschadischsprechenden Ethnien bewohnt ist (Tumak als südlichster Vertreter), stellt man fest, dass die Ablautkräfte allmählich schwinden. Neue lautliche Instrumente, vor allem Affigierung (Agglutinierung) und Ton, drängen nach vorne und verdrängen allmählich das aus dem Osten ererbte Ablautvermögen. Das Gadang scheint noch am konservativsten zu sein, Sumray und Kwang halten etwa die Mitte, Tumak verfügt nur noch über tonale Mittel, auch ohne jedwede Affixausstattung.
tone_statements.translation: Crossing the Chari and entering the land between the rivers (between Chari and Logone), whose upper part (down to about 9 degrees N in the south) is inhabited exclusively by Chadic-speaking peoples (Tumak being the southernmost), one finds that the forces of ablaut gradually fade. New phonic instruments, above all affixation (agglutination) and tone, push forward and gradually displace the ablaut capacity inherited from the east. Gadang still seems the most conservative, Sumray and Kwang hold roughly the middle, Tumak has only tonal means left, without any affixal equipment.
tone_statements.locator: p. 173, section 2 'Der mittlere Osten'; second mention p. 179
tone_statements.summary: Passing typological placement only: Sumray = tonal East Chadic language at a mid stage between ablaut-based and tone-based verb morphology; no tone inventory or rules given (the 3-level H/M/L system remains as stated by Barreteau & Jungraithmayr 1982, a work listed here).

sources.note: An east-to-west tonogenesis narrative for Chadic (ablaut-rich, two-tone-level 'archimorphous' east -> tone-dominant west, up to five levels in Mushere). Sumray is placed at an intermediate stage where inherited ablaut is receding and affixation and tone are advancing ('Sumray und Kwang halten etwa die Mitte'); the three-level count is asserted for the Masa-Zime zone west of the Logone, not stated for Sumray itself. No Sumray examples.
